# **CHAPTER 380**

Walking along a mountain trail at night is dangerous enough as it is.

So this whole “test of courage” thing gives me a fundamentally creepy, unsettling feeling.

A retreat event that makes you go deep into the mountains in the middle of the night… Why on earth does something like that even exist?

*Thud.*

I found myself wondering, ‘...Did those kids who died at the retreat center die in an accident during the test of courage?’ 

I tried to shake the thought off.

*Thud.*

The footsteps of the three of us echoed silently across the dirt path and among the broken twigs as we pressed forward through the darkness.

We had probably walked about 70 meters up the hill.

‘...It’s a crossroad.’

My eyes, now adjusted to the darkness, spotted something among the trees.

“It’s a sign.”

A scruffy green metal sign was stuck in a tree.

I could read it when I got very close.

**《 — Fairy Rock**

Jin Nasol immediately turned left.

‘One of the stamp locations was Fairy Rock, wasn’t it?’

But I noticed another sign behind that one—one that was half-corroded

and hard to make out...

**《 — Fairy Rock**

**~~Shinmaru Retreat Center — 》~~**

An inexplicable chill ran down my spine.

‘Ugh.’

I followed right behind Jin Nasol, as if chasing after her.

The last remaining worker quickly fell in line beside me. He probably feared being left behind.

I could relate to that feeling.

“Excuse me.”

“…Yes.”

Right. It was just the moment I’d thought that walking while talking like this might make it less scary.

“It feels like someone’s following us from behind...”

“......”

“I’ve been hearing footsteps for a while now.”

*Thud.*

Instinctively, I strained my ears.

Beyond the overlapping footsteps of the three of us...

......

*Rustle*

*Thud.*

*Rustle*

"Can you hear that?"

I heard it.

"This is definitely..."

"It must be the other people who came in with us."

"Huh?"

I answered without even taking a breath.

"Since several groups came in, there were obviously other people ahead and behind us in the hallway. It must be one of those groups."

.......

“R-right. A lot of people came in.”

“Yes. That’s definitely it.” 

What does that even mean?

‘This is driving me crazy, seriously.’ 

The horror torture begins…

“So let’s walk faster.”

 “.....”

The worker swallowed hard.

I clamped my mouth shut again and kept walking forward.

“Wait a minute\! Wouldn’t it be better to wait and go together? I mean, in a situation like this, it’s better to have more people around....”

“Oh, really? Then you stay here.”

“....\!”

"Whether you keep your mouth shut or not, just shut up."

Jin Nasol said this without even looking back.

"Why are you whining so much when all you have to do is finish this quickly and go inside?"

"No...."

"Can’t you think straight? Don’t you have the ability to learn?"

"......"

"Wait a minute, Assistant Manager."

 This won’t do.

I approached Assistant Manager Jin Nasol and whispered in a low voice.

“Speaking that way won’t accomplish anything.”

“......”

“Aren’t our situations different?”

“What’s different?”

“Both you and I are currently employees of this branch office...”

“Oh.”

The corners of Jin Nasol’s mouth turned up slightly.

“Who’s going to listen to some cripple who can’t do anything without painkillers?” 

“….\!”

A dry voice came out.

“True, there’s no way they’d listen to someone like that telling them what to do.”

"No."

I replied calmly.

"Because you’re not their superior right now."

"......."

"I think that to persuade someone on the same level, you have to provide a thorough explanation, one they can understand."

A brief silence fell.

And then.

“Right.”

Jin Nasol murmured quietly.

“Both statements are true.”

“...Assistant Manager.”

“I get it. From now on, you do the talking.” 

Jin Nasol didn’t get angry.

With a somewhat stoic gesture, she simply took out another painkiller, chewed it, and swallowed it.

"....."

Amid the fear, a strange sense of confusion welled up and then vanished.

‘Phew.’

I took another step.

The worker quickly followed me again.

“Hey, now that we’re in this situation, why don’t we introduce ourselves? I’m— what’s my number? Y463. I used to run a tteokbokki shop in Busan...”

“You’d better do that outside. I’m so scared right now that I don’t think I’ll be able to remember it even if I hear it.”

“Oh, yeah...”

The worker mumbled, looking a bit embarrassed.

“Haha... Once we’re done with work, I’ll buy some tteokbokki from the snack bar and treat you to a proper serving.”

“.....Thank you.”

 Please don’t do that.

‘Stop laying down all these foreshadowing clues like, ‘Since he was so friendly, like a neighbor, his death would be a huge shock’…’

Doesn’t he seem just like a supporting character in a horror movie who never makes it to the end and gets killed off early...?

“Let’s talk more after we’ve safely made it out first.”

Wait a minute, does that sound like foreshadowing too?

‘Ugh.’

I’d better just keep my mouth shut.

I barely managed to rein in my feet, which were about to break into a run, and continued moving slowly.

*Thud.*

‘...I can barely make out the silhouette anymore.’ 

The deeper we went into the mountains, the darker it became.

Making our way through the pitch black darkness heightened both our tension and our sense of claustrophobia.

Trying hard not to pay attention to the footsteps echoing behind us, we pressed on, and as a result…

"......"

"Stop."

“Yes.”

The narrow path suddenly opened up a bit, revealing what looked like a small clearing.

The dirt ground was slightly easier to walk on.

“Is this a clearing?”

“Probably.”

As we walked a little further, we saw something blocking the mountain path as if it had been cut off abruptly.

Something massive.

“A rock. You check it too.”

At Assistant Manager Jin Nasol’s words, I cautiously reached out and touched what was ahead.

The rough texture of an old rope tied with straw. And then I felt the cold touch of stone....

*Thud.* Something grabbed my wrist.

“......\!\!”

I yanked my arm away violently.

‘Oh my god\!’ 

The sensation of cold, curled fingers scraped against my arm as they fell away. In the process, I bumped into the worker standing behind me.

“What— what’s going on?\!”

I couldn’t let this person see how I was feeling.

Fear was contagious, after all.

“…I just stumbled. I’m sorry.”

“Ah....”

I couldn’t faint, I couldn’t....

‘Pretend you don’t notice.’

Ha.

Gritting my teeth, I slowly stared at the rock.

…I couldn’t see it clearly.

In the darkness, the rock’s surface was submerged in shadow, remaining a source of fear in the realm of the unknown and the imagination…

I desperately longed for the light.

"Check behind the rock. There’s a stamp there."

"...Yes."

I ran my hand over my arm and moved my trembling legs forward.

Just as Assistant Manager Jin Nasol had said, there was an old folding desk sitting alone behind the rock, and on top of it I could see a plastic model stamp and an instruction sheet.

| Sageungsan Mountain’s Fairy Rock Legend has it that a fairy dressed in a five-colored winged robe lost her footing on a cloud, fell, and landed on a rock halfway up the mountain. Traces of where the fairy sat remain on the surface of the rock. |
| ----- |

This was the first stop.

I closed my eyes tightly and picked up the stamp.

Dust had accumulated around it, and I could feel its texture on my fingertips.

‘…But the ink hasn’t dried.’

What on earth was it made of?

Suppressing a shiver, I quickly pressed the stamp onto the designated spot on the brochure.

### **A Thrilling Test of Courage**

#### **Collect ~~4~~ *3* stamps and claim your prize.**

*Let’s visit the famous spots on Mount Saegyeong in the darkness of night to build our courage and self-discipline and strengthen our minds.*

**Fairy Rock – Saegyeong Mountain Lodge – Osaek Mineral Spring**

|  Stamp  | ![][image1] |  |  |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |

Prize Pickup Location:

Information Desk in front of the entrance on the 1st floor of the Training Center

One done.

And then.

“Please hold out your arm.”

“Huh? What?”

“Because it didn’t say you had to stamp the paper.”

I stamped everyone’s clothes as well, just in case we lost the paper.

…Maybe because my hand had been grabbed earlier, touching someone else’s body felt a little creepy.

“Let’s move on to the next one, then.”

“…Yes.”

Assistant Manager Jin Nasol set off again without hesitation.

“Since we can’t see clearly, maybe going a little slower...”

“There’s no issue. Walk.”

Yes, ma’am.

It was the moment I thought I might actually cry from gratitude.

*Rustle.*

"...\!"

…The footsteps I’d been hearing for a while came back again.

But they were incredibly close.

‘Right behind me.’

*Rustle, rustle*. I swallowed hard, grabbed the person next to me, and got ready to run...

“Huh? It’s just people.”

“See? I told you I heard footsteps\!”

‘...\!’

I turned my head.

The silhouette emerging from the path... was wearing a work uniform.

“For a big corporation, they sure make us do all kinds of crazy stuff.”

“No wonder their stock price has been tanking lately.”

They were workers.

‘They really were from a different group.’ 

In an instant, my tension melted away.

‘Phew.’

Who would've thought the blind shot I made as an excuse would actually hit the mark like this?

“Huh? Hey, over there...”

“We’re from a different group.”

“Oh, okay. Good work.”

Since they didn’t know who I was, I guess I didn’t need to adjust my tone.

I could see a faint silhouette that seemed to have noticed us and was waving its hand.

Behind them, three other figures seemed to be emerging from the narrow path...

“I guess those are the people who just arrived?”

Wait a second.

“Are you the first group to enter?”

“Uh, yeah. Wait, are you still getting your first stamp? We’ve already gone and gotten one from somewhere else too.”

“…Where did you get your stamp?”

“Uh, in the spring. We even took a sip of the spring water, ahh\~ it was so refreshing. It felt like my headache and toothache just vanished.”

...They were doing a test of courage on a hillside and actually drank the water coming out of there?

‘They’ve got some guts...’

Wait, or do I just know too much?

Holding back a sigh, I glanced over to see if the people who had completely emerged from the narrow path were moving.

One, two, three, four.

…Four?

"Where is the other one?"

"Huh?"

"There were five people per group, weren't there?"

"Oh, yeah."

One figure shrugs.

Then he makes a gesture as if opening something with his hand.

"Well, he said he'd be back after smoking a cigarette, but was late, so I just left him there."

…\!

To smoke a cigarette, you have to light a lighter.

‘If that’s the case, then that person…’

Must have lit a lighter.

Even though I told myself it was a relief that it was just one person, it was still a bitter and frightening thought.

Especially since the rest of the group had no idea.

“Not like they’re kids. They’ll figure it out and follow on their own.”

‘Phew.’

“Anyway, that’s why these chainsmoking brats are no good.”

.......

Wait a minute.

No.... Maybe I was overreacting.

“...Brats?”

“Huh? Well, I mean, let’s just be honest here, right? They’re all in the same boat, having hit rock bottom, so what...”

“No. That’s not what I meant...”

I swallowed hard.

‘Kids,’ ‘brats’.

“The suffix ‘-deul¹’… seems to imply there are multiple people, doesn’t it?”

“Oh, right.” 

A listless voice.

“There were just the two of them.”

......

......

I slowly turned my head.

One, two, three, four… 

Still,

There were four of them.

“Anyway, let’s take a stamp too. There’s a stamp over there, right? It’s nice to have each other around now that there are more people.” 

They’re coming closer.

Four people are approaching.

They’re getting close enough that I can make out their shapes.

Three silhouettes in work clothes.

And at the very back…

A silhouette not wearing work clothes.

“...Stop right there.”

One.

“Huh?”

“What did you say?”

I pointed at the person at the very back.

“You, I said stop.”

“What the hell is this guy talking about?”

“What’s your number?”

“Ah\~ what the hell, asking a guy for his number?”

“I mean your work number.”

“Work number?”

“.......”

“.......”

"Sir, what's your worker number?" 

Damn it.

"What the hell\!"

It was a voice strained into an unnaturally high pitch, like something trying far too hard to mimic a child.

My body went rigid. The other three with me flinched in terror and spun toward the fourth figure.

"You, you—who are you?\!"

*"Huh?"*

"Are you from another group, you bastard? When did you start following us?\!"

*"I’ve been here the whole time,*  
*can’t you see me?"*

"What's up with this guy? His voice..."

"Come this way\! Get away from there\!"

But the other team members ignore me and move around haphazardly. Their silhouettes jostle violently as they scramble this way and that.

"Hey\! Lighter, lighter— you've got one too\! Turn it on\!"

"Don't turn it on..."

It’s too far.

It’s too late.

“Hey.”

Jin Nasol grabbed the back of my neck and spun me around.

“Run.”

I clenched my teeth and started running around the rock.

“Hic\!”

“Wait a sec... uh,”

“Aaaargh\!”

“Jungseok\!”

The sound of a foot slipping.

From beyond the rock, I heard something fall, roll, and then a dull, cracking sound as it shattered.

“Ugh... ugh.”

“F-fire...” 

“.......”

“That was awesome.”

“Whoa.”

*Thud.*

A cracking sound, like a watermelon splitting open.

I tried not to imagine what had broken.

I tried to put distance from the light and what I had witnessed.

Just as a sweet taste began to fill my mouth.

“Oh, a cabin\!”

I saw something else at the end of the road. That silhouette is...

‘A building...\!’

Assistant Manager Jin Nasol ran over, found the doorknob as if by magic in the darkness, and opened it.

We immediately darted inside through the open door.

“Gasp,”

The nameplate brushed right past my nose.

**Sagyeong Mountain Lodge**

*Thud.*

The door closed.

Any faint glimmer of light was completely blocked out.

“Hah.”

I clenched my fist tightly…

*Rustle*

“.....”

A sound right in front of the lodge door.

*Rustle*

“Ugh....”

I clamped a hand over the worker's mouth, while covering my own at the same time. The ragged sound of my breathing escaped between my fingers.

And then.

*Rustle*

The sound moved past the cabin.

*Rustle…*

"......"

"......"

For a while, silence hung heavy inside the mountain cabin, which was completely shrouded in darkness…

'Phew.'

A terrified voice came from beside him.

"W-wait... what was that just now? Did someone die?"

"......."

"Forget the stamp or whatever—I think I need to report this, report it... Ugh\!"

"Here it is. Get me the paper." 

Meanwhile, Assistant Manager Jin Nasol walked through the lodge and found the stamp.

'I admire her...'

Of course, she completely ignored the lone worker from our team who was still there.

“Come on, I told you to wait a moment…\!”

“Watch your step.”

Without shaking off the terrified worker clinging to me, I slowly made my way toward the sound of Jin Nasol's voice. 

To be honest, after what had just happened, staying close to another person felt far less frightening. 

Cold sweat trickled down my spine. I took another deep breath.

As I got closer, I could sense a very faint glow of natural light coming through the window on the opposite side of the mountain hut. From that vantage point, I could make out the general location of the group.

I could just barely make out the silhouette of the stamp mounted on the wall next to the window.

‘So that’s how they recognized it.’

There was no explanatory sign like the one I’d seen earlier at “Saegyeong Mountain Fairy Rock.”

‘Let’s hurry up and get out of here.’

I gritted my teeth and moved my hand quickly to stamp one more time.

### **A Thrilling Test of Courage**

#### **Collect ~~4~~ *3* stamps and claim your prize.**

*Let’s visit the famous spots on Mount Saegyeong in the darkness of night to build our courage and self-discipline and strengthen our minds.*

**Fairy Rock – Saegyeong Mountain Lodge – Osaek Mineral Spring**

|  Stamp  | ![][image2] | ![][image3] |  |
| ----- | :---: | :---- | :---- |

Prize Pickup Location:

Information Desk in front of the entrance on the 1st floor of the Training Center

There was only one thing left.

‘Please, just let this be over already…’

Just as I was muttering that,

“Uh?\!” 

“...?\!”

I thought my heart was going to stop.

Fortunately, the worker was unharmed, but his voice— still trembling with fright—wouldn’t stop.

“The wall over here\! On the wall... there are tons of missing person flyers and posters, and stuff with ghost stories written on them...”

“......”

Since we’re in the middle of a ghost story, of course there’d be stuff like that...\!

‘Stop it....’

And I already know all about it....

I really didn’t want to see that.

‘Of course it’s going to be terrifying.’ 

I wanted to cover the worker’s mouth.

I was on the verge of losing my composure and shouting, “Stop looking and move on,” just like Assistant Manager Jin Nasol.

“....Supernatural Disaster Management...Agency?”

‘..\!\!’

My head snapped around reflexively.

The worker was pointing with his finger at one wall of the mountain lodge—a wall plastered with so many flyers it looked out of place.

As I moved closer, I could make out the text scattered among the large letters.

**Looking for a missing child.**

**Call here for phone repairs\!**

**~~Come to Shinmaru Training Center~~**

The worn-out, old, and tacky flyers, plastered all over the wall like this person’s face, evoked an even greater sense of unease.

But one of them...

As my eyes adjusted to the darkness, a flyer—which had probably once been colorful—caught my eye, even if only in black and white…

**![][image4]**

"..\!\!"

Oh my God.

"Hey, aren't we in exactly that situation right now? Shouldn't we contact them?"

"But we have no way to contact th—..." 

The words died in my throat. 

Beyond the worker, at the corner of the wall, there was a square outline that stood out more than the flyers....

| Sagyeong Mountain Lodge Public Phone ※Please keep calls brief ^^ |
| :---: |

There was.

A way to get in touch.
